title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 2 questions (2.1, 2.2, 2.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An identity holds Role A and Role B, and both roles grant the Active Directory group VPN Users. After a department change the identity no longer meets Role A's criteria but still meets Role B's. What is the outcome after identity processing?
choices: The VPN Users group is removed and then provisioned again on the next refresh
Both roles are removed during identity processing because they grant the same group
Role A stays assigned until a certification campaign revokes it
Role A is removed and the VPN Users group stays because Role B still grants it
questions.answer: Role A is removed and the VPN Users group stays because Role B still grants it
questions.explanation: Access is deprovisioned when a role is lost only if no other assigned role still grants it, so the overlapping group is retained. Nothing is removed and re-added, and the shared entitlement does not affect Role B.

questions.stem: A contractor has no account on a directly connected ServiceNow source. A role that contains a ServiceNow entitlement is assigned to the contractor, and the source has a configured Create Account definition. What is the MOST likely provisioning outcome?
choices: The role assignment fails until an administrator creates the account by hand
ISC creates the account from the Create Account definition and adds the entitlement
The entitlement waits until the next aggregation discovers a ServiceNow account
ISC sends a manual task to the source owner asking them to create the account
questions.answer: ISC creates the account from the Create Account definition and adds the entitlement
questions.explanation: When access is granted on a source where the user has no account, ISC creates one using the source's Create Account definition. A manual task to the source owner is the flat file behaviour, not the direct connect behaviour.

questions.stem: A role was removed from an identity, and it granted the only entitlements on that identity's Jira account, an account ISC originally created through the role. What happens to the Jira account?
choices: The account remains on the source with the role's entitlements removed
The account is deleted because ISC created it through role provisioning
The account is disabled because it no longer holds any entitlements
The account becomes uncorrelated from the identity
questions.answer: The account remains on the source with the role's entitlements removed
questions.explanation: Deprovisioning entitlements never removes the source account, even when role provisioning created it or nothing is left on it. Disabling or deleting accounts is a lifecycle state action, not a side effect of losing a role.

questions.stem: An access request grants an entitlement on an application managed as a delimited file source, and the identity already has an account there. How is the change fulfilled?
choices: The connector writes the change into the next delimited file the source receives
The requester's manager receives a task to update the application
The entitlement owner gets a manual task, with the source owner as fallback
The request is rejected because delimited file sources cannot be provisioned
questions.answer: The entitlement owner gets a manual task, with the source owner as fallback
questions.explanation: ISC cannot push changes to a flat file source, so it creates a manual provisioning task; tasks involving entitlements go to the entitlement owner with the source owner as fallback. The request is not rejected, and the file itself is not edited by ISC.

questions.stem: An engineer deletes a criteria-based role that granted Salesforce permission sets to 300 identities, expecting the access to be cleaned up. What actually happens?
choices: All 300 identities lose the permission sets during the next identity processing
The deletion is blocked until every member has been removed from the role
The role is removed from the identities, but they keep the access it granted
The permission sets are removed only from accounts that ISC itself created
questions.answer: The role is removed from the identities, but they keep the access it granted
questions.explanation: Deleting a role removes the role from identities without deprovisioning its access; the entitlements simply lose their association with the role. To remove the access, change the criteria so nobody matches, let processing deprovision, then delete the role.

questions.stem: An engineer saved new membership criteria on a role at 10:00, but identities that match the criteria and whose attributes have not changed still do not have the role. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: Criteria-based roles need approval from the role owner before each assignment
Role changes apply only when identity processing runs, such as after Apply Changes
New roles are provisioned only to identities that were created after the role was saved
Each affected source must first complete a full, unoptimized aggregation
questions.answer: Role changes apply only when identity processing runs, such as after Apply Changes
questions.explanation: Role changes are not applied immediately; they are calculated during identity processing, which Apply Changes starts for all identities. Criteria-based assignment has no approval step, and aggregation type does not gate role evaluation.

questions.stem: An identity moves into the inactive lifecycle state, which disables Active Directory accounts. The identity also holds Role R, whose criteria require cloudLifecycleState equals active, and no other assignment grants Role R's access. What is the outcome?
choices: The AD account is disabled, but Role R stays because roles ignore lifecycle states
The AD account is deleted because the identity no longer has any active roles
Nothing changes until a manager submits a revocation request for Role R
The AD account is disabled and Role R is removed, deprovisioning its access
questions.answer: The AD account is disabled and Role R is removed, deprovisioning its access
questions.explanation: The lifecycle state disables the account, and because the identity no longer meets Role R's criteria, processing removes the role and deprovisions its access. Role criteria can use the lifecycle state attribute, and disabling is not deletion.

questions.stem: A role uses AND within groups. Group 1 requires department equals Finance and location equals Boston; Group 2 requires title equals Controller. Which identity receives the role?
choices: A Finance analyst based in Chicago
A Boston employee in the Marketing department
A Controller in the Legal department based in Denver
A Finance contractor whose location attribute is empty
questions.answer: A Controller in the Legal department based in Denver
questions.explanation: With AND inside groups, ISC applies OR between groups, so meeting every criterion of either group is enough; the Denver Controller satisfies Group 2. The Chicago Finance analyst meets only half of Group 1.

questions.stem: A role uses OR within groups. Group 1 is department equals Finance or department equals Accounting; Group 2 is location equals Boston or location equals Austin. Which identity receives the role?
choices: A Finance employee based in Denver
An Accounting employee based in Austin
A Sales employee based in Boston
An Accounting employee with no location value
questions.answer: An Accounting employee based in Austin
questions.explanation: When OR is chosen within groups, ISC joins the groups with AND, so the identity must meet at least one criterion from each group. Only the Austin Accounting employee does; the Denver Finance employee fails Group 2.

questions.stem: Role criteria use Lifecycle State equals Full Time Employee, which is the lifecycle state's display name; its technical name is fte. No identities receive the role. What should the engineer change?
choices: Change the operation from Equals to Contains
Run an unoptimized aggregation of the authoritative source
Switch the criteria type from Standard Criteria to Identity List
Enter the lifecycle state's technical name in the Value field
questions.answer: Enter the lifecycle state's technical name in the Value field
questions.explanation: Role criteria on the Lifecycle State attribute must use the state's technical name, which is the value stored in cloudLifecycleState. Contains would still compare against fte, and re-aggregating does not change the stored value.

questions.stem: A role must go to seven named board liaisons who share no common attribute in HR data, and the group changes rarely. Which assignment approach BEST fits?
choices: Standard criteria on department with seven OR values
An Identity List criteria type that names the seven identities
A lifecycle state that grants the role's access profiles
An entitlement criterion on a group the liaisons do not hold yet
questions.answer: An Identity List criteria type that names the seven identities
questions.explanation: Identity List lets you select specific identities manually when no data-driven rule describes the population. Department values would sweep in everyone in those departments, and a lifecycle state applies to every identity in that state.

questions.stem: A Role Admin needs to take a criteria-assigned role away from one contractor, but no revoke option is offered for that assignment. What is the correct way to remove it?
choices: Ask the contractor's manager to submit a revocation request in Request Center
Delete the role and recreate it so the contractor is not included
Remove the entitlements on the target system and wait for the next aggregation
Change the criteria or the contractor's data so they stop matching
questions.answer: Change the criteria or the contractor's data so they stop matching
questions.explanation: Auto-assigned roles cannot be manually revoked; they follow the criteria, so the identity must stop matching. Deleting and recreating the role would not deprovision anything, and native removal leaves the role assignment in place.

questions.stem: An HR aggregation changes an employee's department from Sales to Support, and the Support department has a criteria-based role. No administrator takes any action. What MOST likely happens?
choices: Nothing changes until an administrator selects Apply Changes on the Roles page
The employee keeps the Sales role until the next certification campaign closes
Event-based processing adjusts the role assignments and provisions the change
The Support role is assigned only after the employee's manager approves it
questions.answer: Event-based processing adjusts the role assignments and provisions the change
questions.explanation: When identity attributes change, event-based processing recalculates role membership and provisions the access changes. Apply Changes is needed for configuration changes to roles, not for attribute changes on individual identities.

questions.stem: A role criterion uses department Equals with the two values Sales and Marketing entered in the Value field. Which identities match this criterion?
choices: Only identities whose department value contains both words
Only identities whose department equals the last value entered
Identities whose department is Sales or whose department is Marketing
Identities whose department starts with the first value entered
questions.answer: Identities whose department is Sales or whose department is Marketing
questions.explanation: Multiple values in an Equals criterion are compared as OR operations, so either department matches. Contains and Starts With are separate operations with different behaviour.

questions.stem: A help desk analyst with the Helpdesk user level is asked to revoke a requested role from a user in the Admin UI. Which access is needed to revoke the assignment there?
choices: Helpdesk, because it can already manage identity access
Admin, Role Admin, or Role Sub-Admin access to that role
Source Admin for any source that supplies the role's entitlements
Cert Admin, because revocation is a certification decision
questions.answer: Admin, Role Admin, or Role Sub-Admin access to that role
questions.explanation: Requested role assignments can be revoked by someone with Admin, Role Admin or Role Sub-Admin access to the role. Source Admin and Cert Admin govern other objects and do not grant role revocation.

questions.stem: A user requested and was granted the Treasury Analyst role, which has no assignment criteria. The user later transfers to Marketing. What happens to the role?
choices: It is removed at the next identity processing because the department changed
It is suspended until the user's new manager approves it again
It is converted into individually requested entitlements on the user's accounts
It stays until revoked by request, certification, lifecycle state or an admin
questions.answer: It stays until revoked by request, certification, lifecycle state or an admin
questions.explanation: A requested role is not tied to criteria, so attribute changes do not remove it; it must be revoked by a removal request, a certification, a lifecycle state or an administrator. That is why movers often keep requested access unless the design handles it.

questions.stem: A manager wants to remove a requested role from a direct report today, without waiting for a certification campaign and without administrator help. What should the manager do?
choices: Revoke the assignment from the Roles page in the Admin UI
Edit the role's membership criteria to exclude the team member
Ask the source owner to remove the account on the target system
Submit an access removal request for the team member
questions.answer: Submit an access removal request for the team member
questions.explanation: Managers can revoke requested access for their team members through revocation (removal) requests. The Roles page needs Admin or Role Admin rights, and editing criteria has no effect on a requested assignment.

questions.stem: A user holds two assignments of the same requestable role, each targeting a different account on the same source. The administrator must revoke only the assignment on the second account. What should the administrator do?
choices: In View Assignments, check the account target details and revoke that assignment
Revoke the whole role, then submit a new request for it on the first account only
Remove the second account from ISC so its assignment disappears
Change the role's multiple account options to point at the first account
questions.answer: In View Assignments, check the account target details and revoke that assignment
questions.explanation: When a user has more than one assignment of a role, verify the account target details before choosing Revoke Assignment so the intended access is removed. Removing the account from ISC only lasts until the next aggregation.

questions.stem: An administrator revoked a requested role from a user, and the user says no email arrived. An auditor asks how the revocation is evidenced. Which statement is accurate?
choices: The user is emailed only after the role owner approves the revocation
Administrative revocations are not audited because an administrator performed them
The notification goes to the role owner, who must confirm it before removal
No notification is sent, but the revocation is captured in audit records
questions.answer: No notification is sent, but the revocation is captured in audit records
questions.explanation: ISC does not send a notification for an administrative revocation, but the action is recorded for audit. There is no role-owner confirmation step for an administrator's revoke.

questions.stem: A requested role contains an Active Directory group and an entitlement on a delimited file application. The role is revoked. How is the access removed?
choices: AD removal is automatic; a manual task is created for the flat file entitlement
Both entitlements are removed automatically through the virtual appliance
Both entitlements require manual tasks because the role mixes source types
Only the AD group is removed; flat file access must be certified away separately
questions.answer: AD removal is automatic; a manual task is created for the flat file entitlement
questions.explanation: Revocation of a role's entitlements is automatic on directly connected sources and becomes a manual task where ISC cannot push changes. Mixing source types does not force everything to manual.

questions.stem: An engineer needs a requestable role to require approval from the role owner and then from a governance group. Where is this configured?
choices: In the role's Access Requests settings, where its approvers are defined
In the identity profile used by the identities that will request the role
On the Create Account definition of each source in the role
In the access profile list of the requesters' lifecycle state
questions.answer: In the role's Access Requests settings, where its approvers are defined
questions.explanation: Requestability and the review process for a role are set on the role itself. Identity profiles and Create Account definitions control identity data and new accounts, not request approvals.

questions.stem: Role change propagation is disabled. An engineer removes an Active Directory group from a role with 500 members and selects Apply Changes. What is the outcome for the members?
choices: They keep the AD group, which is simply no longer associated with the role
They lose the AD group during the identity processing that follows
They lose the group only on AD accounts that ISC itself created
ISC launches a certification for the 500 members to decide on the group
questions.answer: They keep the AD group, which is simply no longer associated with the role
questions.explanation: With propagation disabled, removing access from a role definition does not deprovision it from identities; removal would need a certification or other revocation. ISC does not auto-launch a campaign for this.

questions.stem: Role change propagation is enabled. An engineer removes the Finance Reports access profile from the Finance Analyst role. Some members also hold the Controller role, which includes the same access profile. What happens?
choices: Members lose the access profile's entitlements unless another assigned role still grants them
All members keep the entitlements because propagation affects only additions
All members lose the entitlements, including those who hold the Controller role
Members lose the access profile, but its entitlements stay on their accounts
questions.answer: Members lose the access profile's entitlements unless another assigned role still grants them
questions.explanation: With propagation enabled, removing an access profile from an enabled role deprovisions its entitlements, except where an overlapping role still grants them. Propagation governs removals, not additions.

questions.stem: Role change propagation is enabled. An engineer edits a role at 09:00 to remove an entitlement and nobody selects Apply Changes. When will the removal be processed?
choices: Immediately when the role is saved, without identity processing
Only after the next full aggregation of each affected source
In the daily 6:00 PM tenant-time identity processing
Never, because removals require someone to select Apply Changes
questions.answer: In the daily 6:00 PM tenant-time identity processing
questions.explanation: Identity processing that propagates role changes runs daily at 6:00 PM tenant time and can be started earlier with Apply Changes. Aggregation does not drive role propagation.

questions.stem: With role change propagation enabled, an engineer disables a role, removes two entitlements from it, and re-enables it a week later. What happens to members' access to those two entitlements?
choices: The removals are not propagated, so members keep that access
The removals propagate as soon as the role is enabled again
Members lost all of the role's access when the role was disabled
The edit is rejected because a disabled role cannot be changed
questions.answer: The removals are not propagated, so members keep that access
questions.explanation: Propagation applies only to enabled roles, and access changes made while a role is disabled are not propagated when it is later enabled. Disabling a role does not strip its members' access either.

questions.stem: An engineer must retire a criteria-based role and remove the access it granted, while keeping access that users still need. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Delete the role, since deletion deprovisions its access when propagation is enabled
Change the role's criteria so nobody matches, let processing deprovision, then delete the role
Disable the role and then remove its access items while it is disabled
Remove each member's accounts on the sources and then delete the role
questions.answer: Change the role's criteria so nobody matches, let processing deprovision, then delete the role
questions.explanation: Deleting a role never deprovisions its access, and changes on a disabled role do not propagate, so the role must first lose its members through criteria. Any access users should keep belongs in a new role assigned beforehand.

questions.stem: Role change propagation is disabled. An engineer adds a new entitlement to a criteria-based role and selects Apply Changes. What happens?
choices: Members receive it, because propagation governs only removals
Nothing happens because propagation is disabled for the tenant
Only identities that join the role from now on receive the entitlement
Members must request the new entitlement before it is provisioned
questions.answer: Members receive it, because propagation governs only removals
questions.explanation: Role change propagation does not affect access additions, so identity processing provisions new role access to existing members. The setting controls only whether removals from role definitions deprovision access.

questions.stem: An engineer plans a dozen role, access profile and application edits over one afternoon. What is the recommended way to use Apply Changes?
choices: Select it once, when the whole set of changes is ready
Select it after every single edit to isolate any failures
Select it separately on the roles, access profiles and applications pages
Avoid it and wait for the next authoritative source aggregation
questions.answer: Select it once, when the whole set of changes is ready
questions.explanation: Apply Changes starts identity processing for all identities, and selecting it on roles, access profiles or applications processes all three, so SailPoint recommends waiting until the full set is ready. Running it after each edit repeats tenant-wide processing.

questions.stem: The terminated lifecycle state has Remove all access enabled. A leaver holds requested roles, a birthright role and an access profile granted by the terminated state itself. What access remains after processing?
choices: Nothing; every role, access profile and entitlement is removed
Only the requested roles, until their approvers confirm the removal
Only entitlements on flat file sources, which need manual tasks
Access from birthright roles and from the terminated state's own access profiles
questions.answer: Access from birthright roles and from the terminated state's own access profiles
questions.explanation: Remove all access revokes roles, access profiles and entitlements, but identities keep access from birthright roles and from access profiles provisioned by the current lifecycle state. Removal approvals are bypassed rather than awaited.

questions.stem: Some entitlements require approval to be removed. A leaver enters a lifecycle state with Remove all access enabled. What happens to those approval requirements?
choices: Each removal waits for the entitlement owner's approval
They are bypassed automatically for the lifecycle state removal
The removal is skipped for those entitlements and logged as an error
The leaver's manager receives one combined approval for all items
questions.answer: They are bypassed automatically for the lifecycle state removal
questions.explanation: When Remove all access applies, any approval normally required for removal is automatically bypassed so leaver access is removed promptly. Waiting on approvers would defeat the purpose of a leaver control.

questions.stem: An engineer wants a custom leaver lifecycle state to delete accounts on a SaaS source that supports deletion, but the delete setting cannot be configured. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Account deletion is supported only for delimited file sources
The lifecycle state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
The source's Create Account definition has no password generator
The tenant's account deletion threshold is set too low
questions.answer: The lifecycle state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
questions.explanation: Delete operations can only be configured when the lifecycle state's identity state is Inactive (long-term), and they are also unavailable with the All sources option. The deletion threshold protects aggregations, not lifecycle settings.

questions.stem: The archived lifecycle state deletes accounts on App X. An archived identity still holds a criteria-based role, with criteria that ignore lifecycle state, that includes an App X entitlement. What happens after the next identity refresh?
choices: The account stays deleted and the role is removed automatically
The role is suspended until the identity returns to an active lifecycle state
The App X account is recreated because the role assignment is still active
ISC refuses to delete the account until the role is revoked
questions.answer: The App X account is recreated because the role assignment is still active
questions.explanation: ISC deletes the account, but the active role assignment causes it to be recreated on the next refresh, which is why SailPoint recommends removing related roles before deleting accounts, for example by adding lifecycle state to the role criteria.

questions.stem: The active lifecycle state grants the Base Email access profile. An administrator removes Base Email from an identity that is still in the active state. What happens?
choices: The removal is permanent because administrators override lifecycle states
The identity is moved to a different lifecycle state automatically
It is provisioned again while the identity stays in that state
The access profile is removed from the lifecycle state configuration
questions.answer: It is provisioned again while the identity stays in that state
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted by a lifecycle state are enforced while the identity stays in that state, so a removed one is provisioned again. A permanent change requires changing the state's configuration or the identity's state.

questions.stem: The prehire lifecycle state grants Badge Access. The active state grants Badge Access and Email. An identity moves from prehire to active. What is the result?
choices: Badge Access is removed and then provisioned again
Badge Access is removed because the identity left prehire
Badge Access is kept and Email is added
Email is added only after the manager approves it
questions.answer: Badge Access is kept and Email is added
questions.explanation: Access profiles from a lifecycle state are revoked on leaving it unless the new state also assigns them, so Badge Access persists and the active state adds Email. Lifecycle grants do not pass through request approvals.

questions.stem: A leaver's AD account disable failed during a long virtual appliance outage, and the hourly retries were exhausted. The VA is healthy again. Will the lifecycle state disable the account on its own?
choices: Yes; the lifecycle state disables the account again on every identity refresh
No; lifecycle actions run once, so the disable must be driven another way
Yes; the VA replays every queued disable when it reconnects to the tenant
No; the identity reverts to its previous lifecycle state after the failure
questions.answer: No; lifecycle actions run once, so the disable must be driven another way
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state actions such as enabling or disabling execute a single time and are not a persistent enforcement mechanism; retryable errors are retried hourly up to three times. After that, the disable must be driven another way.

questions.stem: HR sends the value Active for every employee, and identities show the status Lifecycle State Does Not Match Technical Name Case. The lifecycle state's technical name is active. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Rename the lifecycle state's display name to Active
Use Contains instead of Equals in the identity profile mapping
Set every identity's lifecycle state manually to active
Apply a lower transform to the cloudLifecycleState mapping
questions.answer: Apply a lower transform to the cloudLifecycleState mapping
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state assignment is case-sensitive against the technical name, so normalizing the source value with a transform is the durable fix. Manual assignment is reset when the source value changes.

questions.stem: An engineer must retire an old criteria-based role and remove its access while users keep what they still need. Put the steps in order.
items: Define and assign a new role with the access users should keep
Change the old role's criteria so that no identities match
Let identity processing revoke the old role and deprovision its access
Verify on sample identities that only the intended access was removed
questions.explanation: Users first receive the replacement access, then the old role loses its members so its access is deprovisioned. The role is deleted last because deleting it never removes access on its own.

questions.stem: Role change propagation is enabled. Which TWO changes deprovision access from the members of an enabled role?
choices: Removing an access profile from the role
Removing entitlements from an access profile used by the role
Deleting the role
Removing entitlements from the role while it is disabled
Adding a new entitlement to the role
answers: Removing an access profile from the role
Removing entitlements from an access profile used by the role
questions.explanation: With propagation on, removing access items from an enabled role, including from its access profiles, deprovisions them. Deleting a role never deprovisions, changes on disabled roles do not propagate, and additions are not removals.

questions.stem: Match each way an identity can hold access to how that access is normally removed.

pairs.match: Removed when the identity no longer meets the criteria
Removed when the identity is taken off the list

pairs.item: Role granted through an access request
pairs.match: Removed by a revocation request, certification or administrator

pairs.item: Access profile granted by a lifecycle state
pairs.match: Removed when the identity leaves that state, unless the new state grants it

targets_extra: Removed automatically when its source completes a full aggregation
questions.explanation: Each assignment type has its own removal path: criteria and lists are recalculated by identity processing, requested access must be revoked, and lifecycle grants follow the state. Aggregation alone does not remove assigned access.

questions.stem: In a Create Account definition, the mail attribute uses a Static Velocity template that references $sAMAccountName, but new accounts get an empty mail value. sAMAccountName is listed after mail. What is the cause?
choices: Static mappings can hold only literal text and cannot use Velocity
Static templates must reference attributes with the $(name) pattern syntax
Attribute sync must be enabled for any attribute a template references
The referenced attribute is calculated after mail, so it has no value yet
questions.answer: The referenced attribute is calculated after mail, so it has no value yet
questions.explanation: Create Account attributes are calculated in list order, and a Static template can reference only attributes defined higher in the list, so sAMAccountName must move above mail. Static values do support Velocity.

questions.stem: An engineer wants a new account's description to read Dept: followed by the identity's department, but the UI's Static mapping cannot reference identity attributes. What is the BEST way to build this value?
choices: Use a Static mapping with $(department) inside the template text
Map description to the department attribute and add the prefix in attribute sync
Add the prefix to the account schema's display settings for description
Define the field through the provisioning policy API using a transform
questions.answer: Define the field through the provisioning policy API using a transform
questions.explanation: Static values cannot reference identity attributes, so logic that combines text with identity data is set through the provisioning policy API with a transform. Attribute sync copies values as-is and cannot add text.

questions.stem: A SaaS target's create API rejects any request that contains the costCenter field, but the team wants costCenter kept in the account schema for aggregation. What should the engineer do in Create Account?
choices: Remove costCenter from the account schema entirely
Map costCenter to a Static empty value
Set the costCenter mapping to Disable so it is omitted at creation
Mark costCenter as the account's Account ID attribute
questions.answer: Set the costCenter mapping to Disable so it is omitted at creation
questions.explanation: The Disable mapping type omits an attribute when creating new accounts without touching the schema used by aggregation. A static empty value still sends the field, which the API rejects.

questions.stem: An engineer adds employeeType through Create New Attribute in Create Account. New accounts on the target receive the value, but employeeType never appears on the accounts in ISC. Why?
choices: Created attributes are provisioned only once and then discarded by ISC
Attributes added through Create New Attribute require attribute sync to display
The attribute is not in the account schema, so aggregation does not read it
The value is hidden until the source's correlation configuration includes it
questions.answer: The attribute is not in the account schema, so aggregation does not read it
questions.explanation: A newly created Create Account attribute is not included in aggregations unless it is also added to the account schema. Attribute sync and correlation do not control which attributes aggregation collects.

questions.stem: New Active Directory accounts fail with an error that the parent container does not exist. The distinguishedName mapping still reads CN=$(firstname).$(lastname)$(uniqueCounter),OU=YOURCONTAINER,DC=YOURDOMAIN. What is the fix?
choices: Remove $(uniqueCounter) from the distinguishedName pattern
Switch the distinguishedName mapping from Generator to Identity Attribute
Replace the placeholder OU and DC values with the real container path
Add the container name to the AD source's group schema
questions.answer: Replace the placeholder OU and DC values with the real container path
questions.explanation: The default AD pattern ships with placeholder OU and DC values that must be changed to an existing container. The counter only keeps names unique and does not cause a missing-container error.

questions.stem: An engineer needs to change how account attributes are mapped for new accounts on a directly connected source. Where in the Admin UI is this done?
choices: Admin > Identities > Identity Profiles > the profile > Mappings
Admin > Connections > Sources > the source > Account Management > Create Account
Admin > Access Model > Roles > the role > Define Assignment
Admin > Connections > Sources > the source > Account Schema
questions.answer: Admin > Connections > Sources > the source > Account Management > Create Account
questions.explanation: Create Account under the source's Account Management section holds the account attribute mappings used when ISC creates accounts. Identity profile mappings build identity attributes, and the schema only lists account attributes.

questions.stem: A birthright access profile includes access on an application managed as a delimited file source, and a new joiner has no account there. What does ISC do with the Create Account definition?
choices: It ignores the definition because flat file sources cannot create accounts
It writes a new row into the delimited file on the next upload
It holds the access until the joiner's account appears in a later file
It creates a task for the source owner with the computed attribute values
questions.answer: It creates a task for the source owner with the computed attribute values
questions.explanation: Because ISC cannot push changes to a flat file source, it creates a task with the account's attribute values, assigns it to the source owner and emails them. The definition is still used to compute those values.

questions.stem: The sAMAccountName mapping uses Create Unique Account ID with the pattern $(firstname).$(lastname)$(uniqueCounter). An account for John Smith already exists and a second John Smith joins. What value does the second account receive?
choices: The same name pattern with a counter number added to make it unique
An error, because the pattern produces a duplicate value
A random suffix chosen from the source's password policy
The first John Smith's value, with the old account renamed
questions.answer: The same name pattern with a counter number added to make it unique
questions.explanation: $(uniqueCounter) adds a number only when needed to make the generated value unique. Without the counter variable the generator has no way to resolve the collision.

questions.stem: A generator pattern for the mail attribute uses $(sAMAccountName), which is another attribute in the same Create Account definition, and the value comes out wrong. Why?
choices: Generator patterns run before the account schema is loaded
Generator patterns accept only literal text and $(uniqueCounter)
sAMAccountName must first be marked as the Account ID before a pattern can use it
Patterns can use identity attributes but not other Create Account attributes
questions.answer: Patterns can use identity attributes but not other Create Account attributes
questions.explanation: Generator patterns use $(technicalName) for identity attributes and cannot reference other Create Account attributes. To build on another account attribute, use a Static Velocity template listed below it.

questions.stem: A pattern uses $(Family Name) to insert the identity's surname, and generated values contain no surname. What should the engineer change?
choices: Wrap the display name in quotation marks inside the pattern
Use the attribute's technical name, such as $(lastname)
Switch the mapping type from Generator to Disable
Add Family Name to the source's account schema
questions.answer: Use the attribute's technical name, such as $(lastname)
questions.explanation: Patterns reference identity attributes by technical name, shown in parentheses on the identity profile's Mappings tab; Family Name's technical name is lastname. Display names are not valid variables.

questions.stem: The built-in generators cannot meet a requirement to build usernames with custom collision logic. What does SailPoint provide for adding a new generator?
choices: A connector rule that runs on the virtual appliance after creation
A workflow that edits the account after the create completes
An Attribute Generator cloud rule written by the implementation team
A Static mapping that calls an external script to compute the username
questions.answer: An Attribute Generator cloud rule written by the implementation team
questions.explanation: Additional generators are added through Attribute Generator rules, which are cloud rules. Fixing the name after creation with a workflow would leave the account created with the wrong value first.

questions.stem: New AD accounts need a random initial password that satisfies the source's password requirements. Which Create Account mapping is MOST appropriate?
choices: A Static mapping with one shared initial password
An Identity Attribute mapping to the employee number
A password generator mapping on the password attribute
A Create Unique Account ID generator on the password attribute
questions.answer: A password generator mapping on the password attribute
questions.explanation: A password generator produces a random value that follows the configured password policy. A shared static or predictable password is a security weakness, and the unique ID generator is meant for identifiers.

questions.stem: Generated usernames sometimes collide with accounts that administrators created natively in the target yesterday, causing create failures. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: ISC's account data was stale since those accounts had not been aggregated yet
The generator checks uniqueness only against identities, never against accounts
$(uniqueCounter) is ignored when the target is reached through a VA
Unique values are reserved per identity profile rather than per source
questions.answer: ISC's account data was stale since those accounts had not been aggregated yet
questions.explanation: The generator relies on the account data ISC holds for the source, so accounts created natively since the last aggregation are invisible to it. Frequent aggregation, or a generator rule that checks the target, reduces collisions.

questions.stem: A sAMAccountName pattern of $(firstname)$(lastname)$(uniqueCounter) fails for employees with long names. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Remove $(uniqueCounter) so the generated value is shorter
Map sAMAccountName to the identity's email address instead
Use transforms that shorten the name parts to fit AD's length limit
Move sAMAccountName to the bottom of the Create Account list so it is computed last
questions.answer: Use transforms that shorten the name parts to fit AD's length limit
questions.explanation: sAMAccountName has a short length limit, so the name parts must be truncated, for example with substring logic, while keeping a counter for uniqueness. Removing the counter brings back collisions, and an email address is usually too long as well.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to sync the title account attribute on an LDAP source, but title is not listed as eligible on the Attribute Sync page. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: title is not marked as the account's Account ID in the account schema
title is not mapped directly from an identity attribute in Create Account
Attribute sync works only on the authoritative source used by the identity profile
The source must have a Before Provisioning rule before it can sync
questions.answer: title is not mapped directly from an identity attribute in Create Account
questions.explanation: An account attribute is eligible for sync only when it is in the source's Create Account definition and mapped directly from an identity attribute. The Account ID flag and rules play no part in eligibility.

questions.stem: An engineer tries to sync each user's manager to an AD account attribute using the built-in Manager identity attribute and finds it cannot be selected. What is the supported approach?
choices: Create a custom identity attribute for the manager and sync that attribute
Map the built-in Manager attribute through a Static template in Create Account
Enable manager correlation on the AD source to push the value
Use a lifecycle state that grants the manager value as an access profile
questions.answer: Create a custom identity attribute for the manager and sync that attribute
questions.explanation: The built-in Manager attribute can be used in Create Account but not for attribute sync, so SailPoint recommends a custom identity attribute populated with the manager name. Manager correlation finds managers; it does not write values.

questions.stem: After enabling attribute sync for department on an LDAP source, most accounts update but several never do. Those accounts are uncorrelated. Why are they not updated?
choices: Attribute sync applies only to accounts correlated to identities
Uncorrelated accounts are synced only during an unoptimized aggregation
Attribute sync processes accounts in batches and skips older ones
Uncorrelated accounts sync only after the bulk Sync is run three times
questions.answer: Attribute sync applies only to accounts correlated to identities
questions.explanation: Attribute sync enforces identity data on correlated accounts; an uncorrelated account has no identity whose data could be enforced. Correlating the accounts brings them under sync.

questions.stem: An identity has two correlated accounts on the same source, a standard account and an admin account, and the displayName attribute is synced. The identity's display name changes. What happens?
choices: Both correlated accounts are updated
Only the account created first is updated
Only the account chosen by multiple account options
Neither is updated until one account is uncorrelated
questions.answer: Both correlated accounts are updated
questions.explanation: If an identity has multiple correlated accounts on a source, attribute sync updates all of them. Multiple account options choose a target for access profiles, not for attribute sync.

questions.stem: HR data for some users has no mobile number, and after attribute sync is enabled for mobile, existing AD mobile values are being cleared. Why is this happening?
choices: Attribute sync clears any value that it cannot verify against the account schema
AD rejects the update and ISC writes an empty value as a fallback
A null identity attribute value is propagated to the synced account attribute
The bulk Sync resets all synced attributes before writing new values
questions.answer: A null identity attribute value is propagated to the synced account attribute
questions.explanation: When the identity profile mapping sets an identity attribute to null, attribute sync pushes the null to the account. Fixing the mapping, for example with a firstValid transform, prevents the clearing.

questions.stem: A Before Provisioning rule appends a site code to the description attribute, and description is also configured for attribute sync. ISC now keeps trying to resync description. What should the engineer do?
choices: Run the bulk Sync more often so the values settle
Add a second Before Provisioning rule that removes the site code
Change the description mapping in Create Account to Disable
Remove description from the attribute sync configuration
questions.answer: Remove description from the attribute sync configuration
questions.explanation: Attributes that rules change during aggregation or provisioning should usually not be synced, because the identity and account values will never match and ISC loops trying to resync. Running the bulk Sync more often only repeats the loop.

questions.stem: A help desk technician changes a user's title directly in AD, and title is configured for attribute sync with the identity's title from HR. What is the MOST likely result after the next AD aggregation?
choices: ISC updates the identity's title to match the AD account
ISC flags the account for certification and leaves the value as is
ISC ignores the change because only HR aggregations can trigger attribute sync
ISC detects the native change and provisions the identity's title back to AD
questions.answer: ISC detects the native change and provisions the identity's title back to AD
questions.explanation: Attribute sync is triggered when aggregation detects an account attribute changed natively, and ISC may override the change to match the identity. The identity attribute still comes from its identity profile mapping, not from AD.

questions.stem: An engineer has just added three attributes to a source's sync configuration and wants every existing account brought in line. Which statement about the bulk Sync option is accurate?
choices: It can run up to three times per source in 24 hours and only when the source is healthy
It must run nightly because real-time sync does not cover configured attributes
It can run without limits but only when the VA is idle
It runs automatically whenever the account schema changes
questions.answer: It can run up to three times per source in 24 hours and only when the source is healthy
questions.explanation: The bulk Sync is meant for applying newly defined sync configuration, is limited to three runs per source per 24 hours to protect the target, and needs a healthy source. After that, real-time updates enforce sync per account.

questions.stem: A requester submits an access request for an access profile on a source where the target identity has two accounts. How is the receiving account chosen?
choices: ISC applies the access profile's multiple account criteria
The requester picks the account in the request
ISC grants the access to both accounts
ISC always uses the oldest correlated account
questions.answer: The requester picks the account in the request
questions.explanation: For access requests, the requester chooses which account needs the access. Multiple account options on the access profile apply only to automated provisioning through roles and lifecycle states.

questions.stem: A role grants an AD privileged group, and many users have both a standard and an admin AD account. Admin accounts live in an Admins OU. How should the engineer make sure the group lands on the admin account?
choices: Add a role criterion requiring that the identity have two AD accounts
Make the access profile requestable so users pick the account
Correlate only the admin accounts and leave standard accounts uncorrelated
Set the access profile's multiple account options to match OU=Admins
questions.answer: Set the access profile's multiple account options to match OU=Admins
questions.explanation: Multiple account options on the access profile decide which account receives access in automated role or lifecycle provisioning. Leaving standard accounts uncorrelated would break governance of those accounts.

questions.stem: An access profile's multiple account criteria match none of a user's three accounts on a source when a role is assigned. What is the outcome?
choices: ISC grants the access to every account the user has on the source
ISC creates a fourth account for the user from the source's Create Account definition
ISC grants the access to the account that was aggregated most recently
Provisioning fails, or goes to the source owner if manual selection is enabled
questions.answer: Provisioning fails, or goes to the source owner if manual selection is enabled
questions.explanation: When zero or several accounts match the criteria, provisioning fails; with manual account selection enabled, the source owner picks the account through a form in their tasks. ISC does not guess or create another account.

questions.stem: An access profile has multiple account options set to distinguishedName contains OU=Admins. A user with only one account on the source, a standard account, receives the access profile through a role. What happens?
choices: Provisioning fails because the single account does not match the criteria
ISC creates an admin account so the criteria can be met
The single account receives the access; the criteria are not applied
The role assignment is skipped until a second account exists
questions.answer: The single account receives the access; the criteria are not applied
questions.explanation: Multiple account criteria are applied only to users with more than one account on the source. A user with a single account receives the access on that account.

questions.stem: A user already holds an access profile on their standard account and now needs the same access on their admin account on the same source. A request for the access profile is refused. What should the engineer advise?
choices: Create a second identity for the user to hold the admin account
Remove the access profile from the standard account and request it again
Request the individual entitlements, or bundle the access into a role
Change the access profile's multiple account options to include both accounts
questions.answer: Request the individual entitlements, or bundle the access into a role
questions.explanation: An access profile can be associated with an identity only once, so the same access for another account must come from individual entitlement requests or roles. A second identity would break the one-person, one-identity model.

questions.stem: During source onboarding, admin accounts named like adm-jsmith appear uncorrelated, while standard accounts correlate on sAMAccountName. Each admin account stores the owner's employee number in an extension attribute. What is the BEST correlation design?
choices: Correlate the employee number identity attribute to that extension attribute
Rename the admin accounts on AD to match the standard account names
Create a separate identity profile for administrators
Exclude admin accounts from aggregation so they never show as uncorrelated accounts
questions.answer: Correlate the employee number identity attribute to that extension attribute
questions.explanation: Correlation that compares an identity attribute with an account attribute holding the owner's identifier links admin accounts to the right identity. Excluding them hides privileged access from governance, and renaming breaks naming standards.

questions.stem: On a source's Accounts list, one identity appears twice. What does this indicate?
choices: The source has two aggregations still running for the identity
The identity has two correlated accounts on that source
The identity is assigned to two identity profiles
The account was aggregated once from the file and once from the API
questions.answer: The identity has two correlated accounts on that source
questions.explanation: An identity listed more than once on a source has multiple accounts there, possibly with different access on each. That situation is why multiple account options and account selection exist.

questions.stem: When ISC disables an account on a directly connected source, the team also wants a description attribute set on that account. What is the BEST configuration approach?
choices: Add the description to the Create Account definition
Create a provisioning policy with the Disable usage type through the API
Configure attribute sync for description on the source
Map description in the identity profile of the leavers
questions.answer: Create a provisioning policy with the Disable usage type through the API
questions.explanation: Beyond Create Account, provisioning policies for other operations such as Disable and Update are defined through the provisioning policy API. Create Account applies only when an account is created, and attribute sync copies identity values.

questions.stem: The business wants a directly connected source to be governed in ISC, but all account changes must be made by hand by the application team. What should the engineer do?
choices: Delete the source's Create Account definition so changes cannot be made
Remove PROVISIONING from the source's features with the Update Source API
Remove the source from every role and access profile
Set the account deletion threshold to zero for the source
questions.answer: Remove PROVISIONING from the source's features with the Update Source API
questions.explanation: Removing PROVISIONING from the source's features through the Update Source API turns off automatic provisioning, so ISC generates manual work items for the required changes. Deleting the create definition only breaks account creation.

questions.stem: An engineer is scripting a check of whether a source supports automated account changes. What should the script look for?
choices: PROVISIONING in the features list returned by the Get Source API
A non-empty Create Account definition on the source
A healthy status on the source's virtual appliance cluster
At least one entitlement in the source's entitlement catalog after aggregation
questions.answer: PROVISIONING in the features list returned by the Get Source API
questions.explanation: The Get Source response lists source capabilities in its features attribute, and PROVISIONING controls creating and modifying accounts. A create definition or a healthy VA does not prove provisioning is enabled.

questions.stem: An application has no connector, and the company wants account changes for it raised as tickets in its IT service management tool rather than as ISC tasks. Which provisioning channel fits?
choices: A service desk integration for that source
A delimited file source with manual tasks
A workflow that emails the application owner
A Web Services connector with no endpoints configured
questions.answer: A service desk integration for that source
questions.explanation: Service desk integration sends provisioning requests for a source to a ticketing system such as ServiceNow. Manual tasks stay inside ISC, and an email workflow gives no ticket tracking.

questions.stem: Provisioning for an on-premises Active Directory domain is configured in ISC. How does an approved change reach the domain?
choices: ISC connects to the domain controllers directly from the cloud over LDAPS
ISC sends the plan to the source's VA cluster, which runs the connector
ISC writes the change to a file that a scheduled AD script imports
ISC places the change in a queue that AD polls through a web service
questions.answer: ISC sends the plan to the source's VA cluster, which runs the connector
questions.explanation: VA-based sources receive provisioning through the virtual appliance cluster, which runs the connector inside the customer network. The cloud does not reach domain controllers directly.

questions.stem: For one source, the team needs logic that inspects each provisioning plan and conditionally adds or changes attribute requests before the plan reaches the connector. Which option fits?
choices: An Attribute Generator rule on one attribute in Create Account
A Before Provisioning cloud rule attached to the source, reviewed by SailPoint
An identity attribute transform in the identity profile
A correlation rule on the source
questions.answer: A Before Provisioning cloud rule attached to the source, reviewed by SailPoint
questions.explanation: A Before Provisioning rule runs in the cloud before the plan is sent to the connector and can modify it; like other cloud rules, it must be submitted for SailPoint review. Generators and transforms set single values, not whole plans.

questions.stem: An engineer needs to change how a transform-based value is calculated for a field in a source's Create Account definition. Which tool is designed for this?
choices: The Attribute Sync page, editing the sync mapping
The account schema page, editing the attribute type
The identity profile Preview, editing the sample identity's values
The provisioning policy API, editing the field's transform
questions.answer: The provisioning policy API, editing the field's transform
questions.explanation: Fields that use transforms in a provisioning policy are created and edited through the provisioning policy API. Attribute Sync only selects which attributes to keep in sync, and Preview tests identity mappings.

questions.stem: An engineer is enabling attribute sync for a new account attribute on an LDAP source. Put the steps in order.
items: Confirm the identity attribute is mapped in the identity profile
Map the account attribute directly from that identity attribute in Create Account
Select the attribute in the Sync with Identity column on Attribute Sync
Run the bulk Sync once to apply the new configuration to existing accounts
Use View Events to confirm the sync activity
questions.explanation: Sync needs an identity attribute and a direct Create Account mapping before the attribute becomes eligible. The one-time bulk Sync applies new configuration, and View Events opens a search of the sync records.

questions.stem: Match each Create Account mapping type to what it does.

pairs.match: Copies the value of an identity attribute
Computes a value from a pattern, such as a unique ID with a counter
Sets literal text or a Velocity template using attributes listed above it
Leaves the attribute out when the account is created

targets_extra: Keeps the account value updated whenever the identity changes
questions.explanation: These are the four mapping types on the Create Account page. Keeping values updated later is attribute sync, a separate configuration.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about an access profile's multiple account options are accurate?
choices: They apply to access granted by lifecycle states and automated role assignment
When no account or several accounts match, provisioning fails unless manual selection is enabled
They decide which account receives access in an access request
They are applied even when the user has only one account on the source
They default to the account that was aggregated first
answers: They apply to access granted by lifecycle states and automated role assignment
When no account or several accounts match, provisioning fails unless manual selection is enabled
questions.explanation: The criteria drive automated provisioning only, and an ambiguous or empty match fails or goes to the source owner for selection. Requesters choose the account themselves, and single-account users are not filtered.

questions.stem: An engineer has written a new Create Account definition and birthright role for Active Directory. What should happen FIRST before the configuration reaches production?
choices: Enable it in production for one department and watch the results
Run a bulk attribute sync in production to validate the mappings
Ask SailPoint to review the Create Account definition
Test it in the sandbox tenant with test identities
questions.answer: Test it in the sandbox tenant with test identities
questions.explanation: SailPoint's best practice is to test new provisioning configurations in a sandbox environment before enabling them in production. A pilot in production still changes real accounts, and SailPoint reviews rules, not mappings.

questions.stem: An engineer is designing a test for a new criteria-based role. Which test set gives the MOST useful coverage?
choices: Ten identities that all match the criteria in the same way
Every production identity, to see the role's full membership
One identity that matches, since the logic is the same for all
Identities that should match, should not match, and one that stops matching
questions.answer: Identities that should match, should not match, and one that stops matching
questions.explanation: A good provisioning test covers positive cases, negative cases and a mover whose change should trigger removal. Testing only matches misses over-assignment, and testing on all identities is not a controlled test.

questions.stem: In a provisioning test, the account activity for a new AD account shows success. Which step BEST confirms the result end to end?
choices: Close the test because the account activity already shows success
Aggregate the source and confirm the account data in ISC
Run Apply Changes again to make sure the role was evaluated
Check that the identity's lifecycle state is still active
questions.answer: Aggregate the source and confirm the account data in ISC
questions.explanation: Re-aggregating confirms that the target holds the expected attributes and entitlements and that the account correlated back to the right identity. A success status alone does not prove the target data is right.

questions.stem: A provisioning test plan covers new joiners receiving birthright access. Which addition is MOST important before go-live?
choices: Mover and leaver cases that confirm access is removed as designed
More joiner cases with different first names
Performance cases that create thousands of new accounts at the same time
Cases that confirm the email templates use company branding
questions.answer: Mover and leaver cases that confirm access is removed as designed
questions.explanation: Removal paths, such as losing a role on transfer or Remove all access on termination, are where provisioning designs most often fail and carry the most risk. Extra joiner cases add little coverage.

questions.stem: An engineer changed the cloudLifecycleState mapping on an identity profile with 40,000 identities. What should the engineer do before selecting Apply Changes?
choices: Run a full aggregation of every source in the tenant
Disable all lifecycle states until processing finishes
Preview sample identities to check the calculated states
Delete identities whose lifecycle state will change
questions.answer: Preview sample identities to check the calculated states
questions.explanation: Previewing identities shows the calculated attribute values without processing, so mapping mistakes are caught before Apply Changes starts lifecycle provisioning for everyone. Disabling every state would itself trigger unintended changes.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to check a new attribute sync configuration on one test user before syncing a whole source. What should the engineer use?
choices: The bulk Sync option on the source's Attribute Sync page
Synchronize Attributes on that one identity
An unoptimized aggregation of the authoritative source
A certification campaign that includes the test user
questions.answer: Synchronize Attributes on that one identity
questions.explanation: Synchronize Attributes runs an attribute sync for a single identity and analyzes all its accounts. The bulk Sync affects every account on the source and is limited to three runs per day.

questions.stem: Which test case BEST validates a Create Unique Account ID generator that uses $(uniqueCounter)?
choices: One test identity with a long first name
A test identity whose lifecycle state is inactive
Two test identities with the same first and last name
A test identity with no manager assigned
questions.answer: Two test identities with the same first and last name
questions.explanation: Identical names force a collision, which is the only case where the counter must add a number. The other cases do not exercise uniqueness.

questions.stem: A user's access request shows as failed. Where should the engineer look FIRST for the connector's error message?
choices: The identity profile's Mappings tab
The source's account schema
The account activity record for that request
The access profile's multiple account options
questions.answer: The account activity record for that request
questions.explanation: Account activity records hold the status and any error returned for each provisioning action. Configuration pages show settings, not the outcome of a specific request.

questions.stem: An engineer needs a list of every provisioning action that ISC performed on source accounts yesterday, including access requests. Which Search category fits?
choices: Identities
Account Activity
Entitlements
Roles
questions.answer: Account Activity
questions.explanation: The Account Activity category covers most activity that ISC completes on source accounts, such as access requests and other provisioning actions. The other categories describe objects, not events.

questions.stem: A provisioning failure on a VA-connected JDBC source shows only a generic error in the UI. Where is the MOST detailed connector error found?
choices: The tenant's identity processing summary
The email template used for the request
The browser console of the requester
The ccg log on the source's virtual appliances
questions.answer: The ccg log on the source's virtual appliances
questions.explanation: Connector operations for VA-based sources run in ccg on the VA, and its log holds the detailed connector errors. The cloud UI often shows only a summary.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to verify whether attribute sync has actually run for a particular source. What is the quickest way?
choices: Compare the account schema before and after aggregation
Select View Events on the source's Attribute Sync page
Check the source's Create Account definition for changes
Open the identity profile's Preview for one identity
questions.answer: Select View Events on the source's Attribute Sync page
questions.explanation: View Events opens Search with a predefined query that lists attribute sync records for that source. The other pages show configuration, not sync activity.

questions.stem: An access request on an application managed as a delimited file source was approved three days ago and still shows as pending. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: The virtual appliance is offline and queuing the change
The request is waiting for identity processing at 6:00 PM
The connector is retrying a network error every hour
A manual task is waiting for its assignee to complete it
questions.answer: A manual task is waiting for its assignee to complete it
questions.explanation: Flat file sources are fulfilled through manual tasks, so the request stays pending until the assignee completes it. Flat file sources have no VA connection to retry.

questions.stem: The operations team wants to be alerted automatically whenever a provisioning action fails. What is the BEST approach?
choices: A daily export of every identity to a spreadsheet
A certification campaign scheduled each morning
A lifecycle state that emails administrators
A Provisioning Completed workflow that alerts on failures
questions.answer: A Provisioning Completed workflow that alerts on failures
questions.explanation: The Provisioning Completed event trigger fires after provisioning and carries the result, so a workflow can filter on failures and notify. A certification or export would be slow and manual.

questions.stem: After a birthright role is assigned, a user ends up with two accounts on the same source. Account activity shows that ISC created one of them. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: Whether the role's criteria use an AND operator
Whether the existing account was uncorrelated
Whether the source's account deletion threshold was reached
Whether the access profile is marked requestable
questions.answer: Whether the existing account was uncorrelated
questions.explanation: ISC creates an account when the identity has none correlated on the source, so an uncorrelated existing account leads to a duplicate. Fixing correlation before enabling provisioning prevents it.

questions.stem: Creating AD accounts fails with an insufficient access rights error, while aggregation from the same source works. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VA cannot reach the domain controllers
The Create Account definition is missing the password generator
The identity is in an inactive lifecycle state
The service account lacks create rights on the target OU
questions.answer: The service account lacks create rights on the target OU
questions.explanation: Aggregation needs only read rights, but creating accounts needs write permissions on the container. A network fault would also break aggregation, so it is unlikely here.

questions.stem: AD account creation fails because an object with the same name already exists in the container. The distinguishedName pattern is CN=$(firstname).$(lastname),OU=Staff,DC=corp,DC=example. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Move distinguishedName to the end of the Create Account list
Change the mapping type from Generator to Static
Grant the service account domain admin rights
Add $(uniqueCounter) to the distinguishedName pattern
questions.answer: Add $(uniqueCounter) to the distinguishedName pattern
questions.explanation: Without a counter the generator cannot resolve a name collision, so a second person with the same name fails. Static values never vary, and more permissions do not fix a duplicate name.

questions.stem: New AD accounts fail with a constraint violation when the password is set. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The generated password breaks the domain's password rules
The sAMAccountName value contains a counter
The account was created in an OU that is synced
The identity has no manager attribute
questions.answer: The generated password breaks the domain's password rules
questions.explanation: A constraint error at password set usually means the value breaks the domain's complexity or length rules, so the password policy in ISC must meet or exceed the domain's. Counters in usernames do not affect password checks.

questions.stem: A Web Services source returns HTTP 400 Bad Request on account creation, and the target API documentation says lastName is required. ISC's Create Account definition does not include lastName. What should the engineer do?
choices: Change the HTTP method of the create operation to GET
Add lastName to the Create Account definition
Increase the connector timeout on the source
Mark lastName as the source's Account ID attribute
questions.answer: Add lastName to the Create Account definition
questions.explanation: The target rejects the request because a required field is missing, so the field must be provisioned. A timeout change does not fix a validation error.

questions.stem: Provisioning to an AD source starts failing with ConnectException errors, and aggregations also fail. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The Create Account definition has an attribute in the wrong order
The service account's password expired on the target
An access profile's multiple account criteria match no accounts
The VA cannot reach the target system over the network
questions.answer: The VA cannot reach the target system over the network
questions.explanation: ConnectException points to a network path problem between the VA and the target, which affects aggregation and provisioning alike. An expired password produces an authentication error instead.

questions.stem: AD account creation started failing with an error that the parent object does not exist, right after a directory reorganization. The pattern still references OU=Sales. What is the cause?
choices: The OU in the distinguishedName pattern was renamed or removed on AD
The uniqueCounter variable reached the maximum value it can generate on AD
Attribute sync is overwriting the distinguishedName
The role that grants the account is disabled
questions.answer: The OU in the distinguishedName pattern was renamed or removed on AD
questions.explanation: Account creation fails when the container named in the DN no longer exists. Updating the pattern to the new OU fixes it.

questions.stem: Role provisioning for an AD privileged group fails for users who have three AD accounts each. The access profile's multiple account criteria match two of the accounts. What is the cause?
choices: The criteria match more than one account, so ISC cannot pick a target
Privileged groups can only be granted through access requests
ISC grants role-based access only to the first account it ever aggregated
The role exceeds the limit on entitlements per role
questions.answer: The criteria match more than one account, so ISC cannot pick a target
questions.explanation: Provisioning fails when no account or several accounts match the multiple account criteria. Tightening the criteria so exactly one account matches fixes it.

questions.stem: A JDBC source aggregates successfully, but every provisioning attempt fails with a SQL permission error. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: Whether the source's database account can write to those tables
Whether the account schema includes the table's primary key column
Whether the identity profile maps the department attribute
Whether the VA has enough disk space for logs
questions.answer: Whether the source's database account can write to those tables
questions.explanation: Aggregation needs only SELECT rights, so writes failing with a permission error points to the source's database account. Schema and identity mappings do not cause SQL permission errors.

questions.stem: An engineer sees a NoRouteToHostException on an automated role provisioning request. How does ISC handle it?
choices: It retries every minute until the request succeeds
It fails the request immediately without any retry
It treats it as retryable and retries once per hour, up to 3 times
It converts the request into a manual task assigned to the source owner
questions.answer: It treats it as retryable and retries once per hour, up to 3 times
questions.explanation: ISC recognises errors such as ConnectException and NoRouteToHostException as retryable and retries once per hour, up to three times. Endless or minute-level retries would flood the target.

questions.stem: A provisioning action failed with a retryable error at 13:00, and the retry has not run by 14:05. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: Retries run only after the source is aggregated
Retries need an administrator to approve them
Retries are scheduled after 60 minutes but can be delayed by queued work
Retries run only during the scheduled 6:00 PM identity processing each day
questions.answer: Retries are scheduled after 60 minutes but can be delayed by queued work
questions.explanation: The retry is scheduled after 60 minutes but may run later because of other work items in the tenant's queue. It does not wait for aggregation or for approval.

questions.stem: A provisioning request failed because the target rejected an invalid attribute value, which is not a retryable error. What is the correct recovery?
choices: Fix the cause of the error, then trigger the change again
Wait for ISC's three hourly retries to clear the error
Restart the virtual appliance so the failed request is replayed
Delete and recreate the identity
questions.answer: Fix the cause of the error, then trigger the change again
questions.explanation: Only certain connection errors are retried automatically, so a data error must be corrected at its cause before the change is driven again. A VA restart does not replay failed requests.

questions.stem: Attribute sync to a source failed for a day because the target's API was down. The API is back. What should the engineer do to bring the accounts in line?
choices: Nothing, because ISC keeps retrying failed syncs without any limit
Recreate the attribute sync configuration from scratch
Resync affected identities, or run the source's bulk Sync once it is healthy
Run a full aggregation, which pushes the identity values to the target
questions.answer: Resync affected identities, or run the source's bulk Sync once it is healthy
questions.explanation: Failed sync requests are requeued and retried up to 10 times, and after the problem is resolved an administrator can resync identities or run the bulk Sync. Aggregation reads from the target; it does not push values.

questions.stem: A VA was offline for 30 minutes while birthright roles were being provisioned, and the requests failed with connection errors. What is the MOST likely outcome?
choices: The requests are retried and succeed once the VA is back
The requests are lost and the roles must be reassigned
The roles are removed from the identities because provisioning failed
The requests become manual tasks for the source owner
questions.answer: The requests are retried and succeed once the VA is back
questions.explanation: Connection errors are retryable, so ISC retries hourly up to three times, which easily covers a short outage. Failed provisioning does not remove the role assignment.
