questions.stem: A leaver's disable failed on one source and all automatic retries were exhausted. The source is reachable again. What is the MOST direct way to complete the disable?
choices: Wait for the lifecycle state to repeat the disable on the next refresh
Restart the VA so the failed request is replayed
Disable the account from the identity's account actions in ISC
Run an unoptimized aggregation of the source
questions.answer: Disable the account from the identity's account actions in ISC
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state actions run a single time and the retries are spent, so the disable has to be driven again, for example from the identity's accounts in ISC. A VA restart does not replay failed requests, and aggregation only reads account data.

questions.stem: An engineer can meet a provisioning requirement with either a transform or a cloud rule. Which choice is the recommended practice?
choices: Use the cloud rule, since rules run faster than transforms
Use the transform, since cloud rules need SailPoint review
Use both, so the rule can check the transform
Use neither and handle the value in a workflow after creation
questions.answer: Use the transform, since cloud rules need SailPoint review
questions.explanation: Transforms are configurable without code review and are easier to support, while cloud rules must be reviewed by SailPoint before use. Duplicating logic in both invites conflicts.

questions.stem: Account changes on an attribute sync target are often overwritten later by stale values. Which practice from SailPoint's attribute sync guidance BEST reduces this?
choices: Run the bulk Sync several times every day
Disable correlation on the attribute sync target
Aggregate the authoritative and attribute sync sources frequently
Map every account attribute for sync, including attributes nobody uses
questions.answer: Aggregate the authoritative and attribute sync sources frequently
questions.explanation: Frequent aggregation keeps identity and account data current, so sync decisions use fresh values. The bulk Sync is limited to three runs a day and is meant for new configuration.

questions.stem: A new source is being onboarded and will later have provisioning enabled. Which practice MOST reduces the risk of duplicate accounts?
choices: Enable provisioning first and correlate accounts afterwards
Verify correlation while the source is read-only, then enable provisioning
Create every account again from ISC so all accounts are ISC-created and correlated
Skip correlation and rely on attribute sync to match accounts
questions.answer: Verify correlation while the source is read-only, then enable provisioning
questions.explanation: If existing accounts are uncorrelated when provisioning starts, ISC creates new accounts for those identities. Attribute sync works only on accounts that are already correlated.

questions.stem: A provisioning configuration was proven in the sandbox tenant. How should it be moved to production in the MOST consistent way?
choices: Rebuild every setting by hand in production from screenshots
Copy the sandbox's identities and accounts into production along with the configuration
Move the tested objects with configuration hub, then validate in production
Enable the sandbox source in production through a shared VA
questions.answer: Move the tested objects with configuration hub, then validate in production
questions.explanation: Configuration hub lets teams back up and move configuration objects between tenants, which avoids manual drift. Identities are data, not configuration, and should not be copied.

questions.stem: Which practice BEST follows least privilege for a connector's provisioning service account?
choices: Use a domain or global administrator account so that no operation is ever blocked
Grant only the rights its operations need, on the containers it manages
Use the engineer's own account so changes are easy to trace
Share one service account across every source to simplify rotation
questions.answer: Grant only the rights its operations need, on the containers it manages
questions.explanation: A service account scoped to the required operations and containers limits damage if credentials leak. Personal or shared accounts break accountability and widen exposure.

questions.stem: A design uses Create Account to set many attributes once, and the business expects those attributes to stay current as HR data changes. Which configuration completes the design?
choices: Attribute sync for the attributes that must follow identity changes
A second Create Account definition that runs each night against existing accounts
A lifecycle state for each department
A certification that reviews the attribute values
questions.answer: Attribute sync for the attributes that must follow identity changes
questions.explanation: Create Account applies only when an account is created; attribute sync keeps chosen account attributes aligned with identity data afterwards. Certifications review access, not attribute values.

questions.stem: An identity holds a criteria-based role with entitlements on a source that its lifecycle state deletes accounts on. What does SailPoint recommend to avoid the account being recreated?
choices: Remove the related roles from the identity before deleting its accounts
Disable the role for the identity while it is in the leaver lifecycle state
Turn off identity processing for leavers
Lower the account deletion threshold for the source
questions.answer: Remove the related roles from the identity before deleting its accounts
questions.explanation: An active role assignment makes ISC recreate the deleted account on the next refresh, so roles should be removed first, for example by adding lifecycle state to the role criteria. Turning off processing would stop other leaver actions too.

questions.stem: New AD accounts created by ISC are failing. Put the troubleshooting steps in order.
items: Open the failed account activity and read the returned error
Review the ccg log on the source's VAs for connector detail
Fix the root cause, such as the service account's rights on the OU
Repeat the provisioning with a test identity
Aggregate the source and confirm the account is correlated and correct
questions.explanation: Start from the recorded error, deepen with the VA's connector log, fix the cause, retest, then confirm the result through aggregation. Retesting before fixing the cause only repeats the failure.

questions.stem: Which TWO provisioning errors does ISC treat as retryable and retry automatically?
choices: ConnectException
NoRouteToHostException
Insufficient access rights on the target container
Password does not meet the domain's complexity rules
A required attribute is missing from the request
questions.explanation: Connection errors are recognised as retryable and retried once per hour up to three times. Permission, password and data errors need the cause fixed, so retrying would not help.

questions.stem: Match each provisioning symptom to its MOST likely cause.

pairs.item: A second account is created for a user who already had one
A request on a delimited file source stays pending for days
pairs.match: A manual task is waiting for its assignee

pairs.item: ISC keeps resyncing the same attribute
pairs.match: A rule changes an attribute that is also synced

pairs.item: Role provisioning fails for users with several accounts on a source
pairs.match: The multiple account criteria match zero or several accounts

targets_extra: The tenant's API rate limit was exceeded
questions.explanation: Each symptom maps to a documented behaviour: account creation when nothing is correlated, manual fulfilment for flat files, sync loops caused by rules, and ambiguous account selection. API rate limits explain none of these symptoms.
